title: Winning the Esquire award in 1944
summary: With Sabby Lewis he learned in Portland, Maine, that he had won the Esquire poll and received the trophy at the Zanzibar in New York.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I was going to ask you to make a little message to your brothers, if you'd like to. I mean, I'm not... We forgot to mention the Esquire. You might mention that.

Yes. Yes, Esquire. That was in the... I was still with Sabah Lewis' band, see, up in Boston. I didn't know anything about it, told several fans. One night I was up in Portland, Maine, playing a Saturday night dance out on the... the Old Archie, Old Archie Beach. So they asked me, says, gee, I heard you made Esquire. I says, I don't know. He says, sure. And one of the fans had the poll, you know. So, gee, I says, well, I'm glad somebody thought of me. He says, you... Yes, boy. She says, I know everybody. They voted for you. He says, well, that's great. Then, well, then I went from there. We had a job in New York at the Zanzibar. That's where we enlarged the band. We had about 16, 17 piece band because we played the big Zanzibar show, see. And they present the trophy to me there. That's 1944. I was made for Esquire, All-American. The bass player.
